the_ruling_verbatim: oh dear no. the diagnostic inspector and the build inspector are the same mechanism with different data

let me allow one distinction: the diagnostic inspector MUST be a distinct piece of code, but built on the same principles. Why? because all other inspectors can have normal debug logging. but logging for the logging system itself, including its diagnostic inspector... or any other inspector we decide to build for logging... could create circular errors. This is from my experience.
so logging for the logging system itself has to work even if logging iself is broken. but the mechanisms and ideas should be roughly the same.

so far, this is true. but to be clear, this is not physics. i am the first line inspector for my monkey (physical self). my various doctors are my second line inspectors. but i have also trained myself to do that. it is a skill we have not yet tried to create here. but rest assured, we will.
i think an-inspector-may-not-depend-on-what-it-inspects is just ruled against in a terminal manner, but with the reason discussed.
now_the_spec_says: No law forbids self-inspection — a thing can be TRAINED to inspect itself, and Cairn has not built that skill. ONE distinction stands: diagnostic_inspector is DISTINCT CODE from the shared library, same mechanism, different data, so logging for logging survives logging breaking.

reading_correction.what_was_wrong: Two things, and the second is the one that matters. (1) A NARROW ALLOWANCE WAS RECORDED AS A UNIVERSAL LAW. His words say 'let me allow one distinction' and name a single case with a single reason — logging for logging can create circular errors, from his experience. The reading generalized that into 'an inspector may not be built on what it inspects', a prohibition covering every inspector Cairn will ever have, which he never said and on 2026-08-06 ruled against terminally. (2) IT CLAIMED PHYSICS THAT DOES NOT EXIST: 'Guarded by import-scan, never by prose.' Measured 2026-08-06 — `import-scan` appears nowhere in the corpus as code. Every occurrence is an IOU (CLAUDE.md:98, db_domain, inference_domain, intentions_model_compiler, all reading 'once that tooth exists'); the only real one is learning_block's, scoped to its own imports. The line asserting the rule was not prose was itself the only thing enforcing it.
reading_correction.his_counterexample_verbatim_because_it_i: 'i am the first line inspector for my monkey (physical self). my various doctors are my second line inspectors. but i have also trained myself to do that.' A thing inspecting itself is not forbidden — it is a TRAINED skill, backed by a second line that does not share its failure modes. One counterexample is enough to kill a universal, and this one is also a design direction: Cairn has no such training and no second-line tier, which is why the fork exists today.
reading_correction.what_survives_untouched: The diagnostic_inspector fork itself, on exactly the ground he gave it: same mechanism, different data, distinct code, because logging for the logging system must work when logging is broken. He re-affirmed this on 2026-08-06 — 'so far, this is true' — and 'so far' is doing real work in that sentence. It stands as a reasoned distinction, not as a law, and it is expected to be revisited when the trained-self-inspection skill exists.
reading_correction.why_a_general_law_was_the_costly_shape: A universal prohibition forecloses the capability he says we will build. Recorded as law, the next mind reads 'may not' and never asks whether a trained inspector with a second line would be better; recorded as one distinction with its reason, the reason can be checked and can expire. This is the second time in one ruling pass that a specific thing of his was widened into a general one — the other being the inspector subclass collapsed into the learning-block class standard, which he caught only while reading the graph-trees paper for work.

what_is_now_owed_and_is_not_claimed_here.the_scan: If the fork is to be enforced rather than merely stated, an import-scan reding any diagnostic_inspector import of the shared inspection library is the physics. It is NOT built and this packet does not claim it is. It belongs with the other import-scan IOUs, which are a single missing tooth serving five components, not five separate debts.
what_is_now_owed_and_is_not_claimed_here.the_second_line: A second-line inspector tier — something that checks the checker without sharing its failure modes, which is what his doctors are to him — has no design in Cairn. Named here so it is a known absence rather than an unasked question.

supersedes.evidence: Akien, 2026-08-06: 'i said this assertion was conceptually false. it's not physics. it's how things happen to be at the moment. so closed as too divergent from the vision.' The retired packet asserted a universal law ('an inspector may not be built on what it inspects') and claimed physics for it ('Guarded by import-scan, never by prose') that measurably did not exist.
